label: The day after Varna
why: The main reference: the day after the Battle of Varna, the date of the existing 1444 map and country catalogue.

realms.name: Kingdom of England
realms.note: Holds Normandy, Maine, Gascony and Calais; Truce of Tours with France since May 1444.

realms.name: Kingdom of Scotland
realms.note: Minority of James II, Black Douglas ascendancy.

realms.name: Gaelic Irish lordships
realms.ruler: Gaelic and Gaelicised lords (no single ruler)
realms.note: Map grouping for the Gaelic lordships outside the English Pale.

realms.name: Kingdom of France
realms.note: Paris regained 1436; army reform under way during the truce.

realms.name: Burgundian State
realms.note: Holds Burgundy, Flanders, Artois, Brabant, Holland, Hainaut and Luxembourg (1443).

realms.name: County of Provence
realms.ruler: René of Anjou (Count since 1434; lost Naples 1442)

realms.name: Duchy of Savoy
realms.note: Duke Amadeus VIII is antipope Felix V.

realms.name: Kingdom of Navarre
realms.ruler: Juan II (King consort, Blanche I died 1441)

realms.name: Crown of Castile
realms.note: Álvaro de Luna dominant; Olmedo still ahead (1445).

realms.name: Crown of Aragon
realms.ruler: Alfonso V the Magnanimous (resides in Naples)
realms.note: Includes Sicily, Sardinia, Valencia and Catalonia.

realms.name: Kingdom of Portugal
realms.ruler: Afonso V (minor; regent Peter, Duke of Coimbra)
realms.note: Holds Ceuta since 1415; voyages past Cape Bojador.

realms.name: Emirate of Granada
realms.note: Tributary of Castile.

realms.name: Duchy of Milan
realms.note: Last Visconti duke.

realms.name: Republic of Genoa
realms.note: Independent of Milan since 1435; colonies at Caffa, Chios, Pera.

realms.name: Republic of Florence
realms.note: Holds Pisa since 1406.

realms.name: Papal States
realms.note: Eugene IV back in Rome since 1443; Council of Basel and antipope Felix V in schism.

realms.name: Kingdom of Naples
realms.note: Conquered by Alfonso 1442; personal union with the Crown of Aragon.

realms.name: Austria (Habsburg)
realms.ruler: Frederick V (King of the Romans as Frederick III; guardian of Ladislaus Posthumous)

realms.name: Kingdom of Bohemia
realms.ruler: Interregnum: Ladislaus Posthumous recognised, governed by Landfrieden unions
realms.note: Hussite kingdom without a resident king.

realms.name: Bavaria (Wittelsbach duchies)
realms.ruler: Albert III (Bavaria-Munich); Henry XVI (Landshut); Louis VIII (Ingolstadt)
realms.note: Divided into three duchies.

realms.name: Electorate of Cologne
realms.note: The city of Cologne governs itself.

realms.name: Electorate of Saxony
realms.ruler: Frederick II the Gentle with William III
realms.note: Partition of Altenburg 1445 and the Saxon Fratricidal War ahead.

realms.name: Free Imperial City of Lübeck
realms.note: Leading town of the Hanseatic League.

realms.name: Duchy of Pomerania
realms.ruler: Joachim of Stettin; Wartislaw IX of Wolgast; Eric of Pomerania claims Stolp

realms.name: Old Swiss Confederacy
realms.note: At war with Zürich and Habsburg (Old Zürich War); St. Jakob an der Birs August 1444.

realms.name: Teutonic Order in Prussia
realms.note: Prussian Confederation of estates formed 1440.

realms.name: Livonian Order
realms.note: Shares Riga with the archbishop.

realms.name: Kingdom of Denmark (Kalmar Union)
realms.note: Senior kingdom of the Kalmar Union.

realms.name: Kingdom of Sweden
realms.note: Personal union with Denmark (Kalmar Union).

realms.name: Kingdom of Norway
realms.note: Personal union with Denmark (Kalmar Union).

realms.name: Gotland under Eric of Pomerania
realms.ruler: Eric of Pomerania (deposed King of the Kalmar Union)
realms.note: Eric rules Gotland from Visborg castle and wages war at sea.

realms.name: Kingdom of Poland
realms.ruler: Władysław III, killed at Varna on 10 November 1444 (death not yet known; interregnum follows)

realms.name: Grand Duchy of Lithuania
realms.note: Kyiv held by the appanage prince Olelko (Alexander) since 1440.

realms.name: Kingdom of Hungary
realms.ruler: Władysław I, killed at Varna on 10 November 1444; Ladislaus V (child) rival claimant
realms.note: Holds Belgrade; John Hunyadi escapes Varna.

realms.name: Principality of Wallachia
realms.note: Sent troops to Varna; Ottoman tributary in practice.

realms.name: Serbian Despotate
realms.note: Restored by the Peace of Szeged (1444).

realms.name: Albanian lords (League of Lezhë)
realms.ruler: Skanderbeg (leader of the League of Lezhë, March 1444)
realms.note: Skanderbeg won at Torvioll in June 1444.

realms.name: Byzantine Empire
realms.note: Ottoman tributary; Church union of Florence (1439) contested.

realms.name: Despotate of the Morea
realms.note: Constantine rebuilt the Hexamilion and forced Athens to pay tribute in 1444.

realms.name: Duchy of Athens
realms.note: Ottoman tributary; made tributary to Constantine of the Morea in 1444.

realms.name: Ottoman Sultanate
realms.ruler: Mehmed II (first reign), with Murad II, victor of Varna, in command
realms.note: Varna fought on 10 November 1444.

realms.name: Aq Qoyunlu
realms.ruler: Jahangir (sons of Qara Yuluk Osman contend)

realms.name: Qara Qoyunlu
realms.note: Baghdad held by Jahan Shah's rival brother Ispend until 1445.

realms.name: Kingdom of Cyprus
realms.note: Mamluk tributary since 1426.

realms.name: Knights Hospitaller
realms.note: Withstood the Mamluk siege of Rhodes in 1444.

realms.name: Grand Principality of Moscow
realms.note: Civil war with Dmitry Shemyaka; captured by Kazan in 1445 (ahead).

realms.name: Novgorod Republic
realms.ruler: Archbishop Euthymius II and the veche

realms.name: Khanate of Kazan
realms.note: Ulugh Muhammad seized Kazan c. 1438 (traditional 1438; some date it 1445).

realms.name: Great Horde
realms.note: Rump of the Golden Horde.

realms.name: Sharifate of Mecca
realms.ruler: Sharif Abu al-Qasim ibn Hasan ibn Ajlan

realms.name: Rasulid Yemen
realms.note: Rasulid power failing; Tahirids rising.

realms.name: Kingdom of Hormuz
realms.note: Pays tribute to the Timurids.

realms.name: Timurid Empire

realms.name: Moghulistan
realms.note: Kashgar held by the Dughlat amirs.

realms.name: Oirat Confederation

realms.name: Ming Dynasty
realms.ruler: Zhengtong Emperor (Wang Zhen dominant at court)

realms.name: Joseon

realms.name: Ashikaga Shogunate

realms.name: Cambodia

realms.name: Majapahit

realms.name: Delhi Sultanate (Sayyid)

realms.name: Lodi Punjab

realms.name: Bahmani Sultanate

realms.name: Orissa (Eastern Ganga)

realms.name: Marinid Sultanate

realms.name: Mali Empire

paris.note: Retaken from the English in April 1436.

nantes.note: Duchy of Brittany under French suzerainty.

marseille.note: County of Provence under René of Anjou.

dublin.note: Lordship of Ireland (English Pale), governed by the King's lieutenant.

fez.note: Marinid sultan under the Wattasid regent.

algiers.note: Hafsid sphere under local Tha'aliba notables; Zayyanid Tlemcen also claims it.

naples.note: Alfonso V of Aragon, King of Naples since 1442.

palermo.note: Kingdom of Sicily, ruled by a viceroy of Alfonso V.

prague.note: Hussite estates rule in the interregnum; Poděbrady takes Prague in 1448.

cologne.note: The city governs itself; the archbishop-elector resides at Bonn. Formally a Free Imperial City only from 1475.

lubeck.note: Free Imperial City, head of the Hanse.

visby.note: Eric of Pomerania holds Gotland from Visborg 1437-1449.

riga.note: City shared between the Order and the Archbishop of Riga; the city council is largely self-governing.

kyiv.note: Appanage Principality of Kiev under Olelko Vladimirovich (from 1440).

kazan.note: Ulugh Muhammad's khanate; its founding date is disputed (1438 or 1445).

caffa.note: Genoese Gazaria, under the Consul of Caffa.

belgrade.note: Hungarian since 1427; withstood the Ottoman siege of 1440.

athens.note: Duchy of Athens (Acciaioli), Ottoman tributary; tributary to the Morea from 1444 until 1446.

baghdad.note: Held by Ispend, Jahan Shah's rival brother, until his death in 1445.

mecca.note: Sharifate of Mecca under Mamluk suzerainty.

aden.note: Late Rasulid rule, contested; the Tahirids take Aden in 1454.

kashgar.note: Dughlat amirs under the Moghul khans.

lahore.note: Bahlul Lodi holds Lahore and Sirhind as a nominal vassal of the Sayyid sultan.

calicut.note: The Zamorin of Calicut; independent of Vijayanagara.

lhasa.note: Phagmodrupa regime; Lhasa area under its lords.

karakorum.note: Northern Yuan khan Taisun is a puppet of Esen Taishi of the Oirats, who really controls Mongolia.

kamakura.note: Kantō under the Uesugi kanrei; the Kamakura kubo post is vacant until 1449.

hakata.note: Contested by the Ōuchi and Shōni.

angkor.note: Angkor largely abandoned by the court after 1431.

manila.note: Tagalog polities of Manila Bay (Tondo; Maynila); records thin.

timbuktu.note: Tuareg under Akil since 1433; Songhai takes it in 1468.

kanem.note: Bulala hold Kanem; the Sayfawa have moved to Bornu.

great_zimbabwe.note: Great Zimbabwe declining; Mutapa founded to the north c. 1430.

mogadishu.note: Sultanate of Mogadishu; its relation to the Ajuran is uncertain.

gondar.note: Gondar not yet founded; the area is Ethiopian.

azcapotzalco.note: Tepanec power broken in 1428; subject to the Triple Alliance.

mayapan.note: Mayapan abandoned c. 1441; Yucatán split among kuchkabalob (Xiu, Cocom and others).

quito.note: Quitu-Cara chiefdoms, no state; Inca conquest later.

quebec.note: St. Lawrence Iroquoian village of Stadacona, no state.

open_questions: Poland and Hungary: Władysław III died at Varna on 10 November 1444, but his death was not confirmed for months; both kingdoms are shown with him as the (dead) ruler and an interregnum.
Kazan: whether Ulugh Muhammad's khanate dates from 1438 or 1445 is disputed.
Mutapa vs Great Zimbabwe: whether Great Zimbabwe still functioned as a state in 1444 is uncertain.
Mogadishu: whether the sultanate was independent of the Ajuran in 1444 is uncertain.
Algiers: Hafsid, Zayyanid or local Tha'aliba control is unclear.
Karakorum: held by the Northern Yuan khan in name, by Esen Taishi (Oirat) in fact.
Great powers chosen by judgement; England is included for its French holdings despite its decline.

Id harmonisation: the Great Horde continues the Golden Horde (one id, great_horde); the splits are recorded as Kazan, Crimea, Nogai and the Uzbeks forming. Maya continues the League of Mayapan under the map id, now as Maní (Xiu).

Bar is counted as ended when René of Anjou joined it to Lorraine (1431–1441); the Dauphinist kingdom as ended on reunification under Charles VII. Realms still standing were added: Tocco Epirus, Jaffna, Khandesh, Lucca, Montferrat, Riga, Samudra Pasai, K'iche', Quitu-Cara, Tyrol, Siena, Maynila, Mantua, Sicily.
